parsed.answer: Evidence 11899391 directly shows that a Type 1 diabetes-associated IL2RA haplotype correlates with diminished IL-2 responsiveness (reduced STAT5a phosphorylation) in CD4+ T cells and lower FOXP3 expression with reduced suppressive capacity in CD4+CD25+ Tregs, establishing the association in humans. Evidence 13923140 independently links reduced IL-2 (via Il2 haplodeficiency or Idd3 susceptibility alleles) to diminished CD4+CD25+ regulatory T cell function and autoimmune dysregulation in mice, corroborating the Treg/IL-2 axis in autoimmunity, though it addresses IL-2 production rather than responsiveness.
